bullets.text: Calendar-year underwriting margin was 11.9%, down ~3 pts YOY but well above 4% target; net income reached $1.39B; ROE was 25%; 2005 Gainshare score finished at 1.54 versus 1.4 twelve-year average.

The cycle indicates potential decline after peak underwriting margins; 2006 accident-year results may begin producing smaller margins trending toward historical norms, with market conditions showing parallels to the 1998–2000 cycle.
Full-year NPW rose 5% (~$630M) to just over $14B, the smallest gain in five years; auto insurance industry NPW growth estimated at ~1% for 2005, down from 4.2% in 2004.

Adopting annual variable dividend in 2007 based on underwriting profit and Gainshare; share repurchases paused during late-year price run-up to $125 then resumed at $118.92; total portfolio return was 4%.

Practicing deliberate rate restraint rather than immediately pricing away margins; Drive reduced rates modestly and found application growth very hard; Direct kept rates relatively stable and grew new applications at a limited pace.

Prior-period bodily injury severities were generally overestimated; overall favorable calendar-year reserve adjustment was 2.6 points in 2005; expected increases in severity and potentially frequency will slowly absorb margins in excess of target.

Ended 2005 with close to 10 million policies; overall retention measures did not extend at expected rates; deploying statistical process control tools and an employee customer-and-critic program to address customer service 'friendly fire.'

Concierge claims service opened six facilities in 2005, ended the year with 18 under construction, and planned about 30 openings for 2006; the service minimizes repair cycle times and reduces claims handling friction costs.

Marked first full year operating two distinct brands—Drive Insurance for agents and Progressive Direct for direct consumers; entered New Jersey in September offering both brands; celebrated ten years of Web-based business.

Two companywide initiatives face a crucial 18 months: replacing the customer and policy management system, and adding a data center to ensure that capacity is not constrained and high system availability is assured.
